transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello. Well... I suppose my wife is the main reason I'm here. She gets frustrated because I... well, I guess I have this habit of checking things. 

Just... going over the same lists, or checking boxes. The drawers in the condo, mostly. I'll look through them over and over before I can move on to whatever we're doing. I know perfectly well I already looked, but... anyway, she's always just standing there waiting for me to leave it be. So... that's what brought me in.
When you check the drawers, do you have certain thoughts that come to mind that make you feel anxious, or do you do it more out of habit?

Well... I suppose it's not just a habit. It's... there are thoughts. Just these nagging ideas that I might have accidentally thrown away something important. Usually things from my old teaching files, or... maybe that I put a needed tool in the wrong box. 

I tell myself it's highly unlikely, but... well, the thought just comes back anyway. It just makes it hard to settle until I look.

When you have the thought that something important might be missing or misplaced, does it feel like something bad will happen if you don’t check, or is it more about just not being able to shake the thought?

I don't know that I've... really analyzed it like that. I don't think anything terrible is going to happen, exactly. 

It's just... well, the thought is just there. I can't quite drop it. So I look. That's... really all it is.
When you check the drawers or go through your lists, does it feel like you have to do it a certain number of times or in a specific way to feel reassured or prevent something bad from happening?
No, not a certain number. I just... I just look until I feel like I've looked enough. There's no special way I do it. I just check them.
Does this checking behavior cause you a lot of distress, or does it interfere with your day-to-day life in any way?

Well... I suppose it's slowing things down. Unpacking the new condo... it's just taking much longer than it should. 

I... I have some tutoring I do at the library, and my hobbies, but I've been putting them off. It's just... I feel like I can't really move on to those things until I've verified the boxes enough. It's a bit of a nuisance, I suppose.
Do you ever have thoughts that come into your mind that you don’t want or that upset you, like fears of harming someone accidentally or having done something wrong?

Well... no, not like harming anyone. Nothing like that. 

It's more just... I keep getting these nagging thoughts that I might have accidentally thrown away something important. Like some of my old teaching files. Or... or maybe I put a tool I'm going to need in the wrong box. 

I tell myself it's unlikely, but... the thought just keeps coming back. It makes it hard to just sit down and settle. But it's not about hurting anyone.
Do you find yourself repeating any other behaviors over and over, like washing your hands, counting, or arranging things, or is it mainly just checking the drawers and boxes?

No... I don't do any of that. I don't count things, or wash my hands more than normal. 

It's really just... just the boxes and the drawers. That's all.
Do you ever have thoughts that pop into your head that you don’t want or that really bother you, even if you try to push them away?
Well... I thought I just answered that. It's really only what I mentioned a moment ago. Just the worry about tossing out my old files or tools. I don't... nothing else comes to mind.

When you have those worrying thoughts about throwing away something important, do you feel driven to do the checking to prevent something bad from happening, even though you know it's probably not necessary?

Yes... I suppose so. That's, well, that's what brought me in, really. 

I just... I find myself checking the same boxes and lists. The drawers around the condo. I end up looking through them over and over before I can finally move on. 

I know perfectly well I already looked. And my wife is usually waiting for me to just leave it be, but... well. I just check them anyway.
Are these worries about throwing away something important the only kind of unwanted thoughts you have, or do you ever experience other types of intrusive thoughts that bother you?
No... I don't think so. It's just the files and the tools. I don't really have other... thoughts like that. Just the one thing.
Do you ever have other types of intrusive or unwanted thoughts that cause you anxiety, such as concerns about contamination, symmetry, or disturbing mental images?
No... I don't. I think we just went over this. It's really only the files and the tools. I don't have any issues with germs or... whatever else you mentioned. Just what I already told you.
Do you ever find yourself doing anything else, like silently repeating a word or phrase, making mental lists, or trying to 'neutralize' the worry in some way when these thoughts come up?
No... no, I don't do any of that. I don't... talk to myself or make mental lists. I just check the drawers and the boxes. That's all.
Have you ever experienced any intrusive thoughts or worries about something being 'just right,' or felt the need to arrange things in a specific way to make things feel balanced or correct?
No... I don't think so. I don't really care about how things are arranged, as long as they're there. I just... I just check to make sure they haven't been thrown out. That's really all it is.
When these thoughts about throwing away something important come up, do they feel unwanted and bothersome to you, and do they cause you significant anxiety or discomfort?

Yes... they do. I just... I get these nagging thoughts that I might have tossed out some important teaching file, or put a tool in the wrong box. And... even when I tell myself I didn't, the thought just keeps coming back. It... it makes it hard to settle down. It's bothersome, yes.
Have you ever had any intrusive or unwanted thoughts that are aggressive, sexual, or religious in nature, or thoughts that upset you greatly and don’t seem to fit with who you are?
No. No... definitely not. I don't have... thoughts like that. Nothing of that nature. Like I said, it's really just the worrying about tossing out my old files or tools. That's all it is.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits recurrent and persistent intrusive thoughts related to potentially misplacing important items (e.g., teaching files, tools), which he recognizes as his own thoughts and which cause him distress and functional impairment. He engages in repetitive checking behaviors (e.g., checking drawers and boxes) in response to the obsessions, though not in a ritualized or compulsive manner. There is no evidence of additional intrusive thought themes (e.g., contamination, symmetry, aggression, or sexual/religious content), nor are there ritualized compulsions or a requirement for things to feel 'just right.' The duration of symptoms appears to be chronic and ongoing, with functional impairment related to daily tasks and hobbies.
